profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This CyrusOne campus sits in Loudoun County, Virginia, in and around Sterling, part of the Northern Virginia Ashburn area data center corridor. Wikipedia coverage of CyrusOne states the company purchased 40 acres in Loudoun County in June 2016 for data center construction. CyrusOne was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten, went public in 2013, and was taken private in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts and Global Infrastructure Partners acquired it for 15 billion dollars. No building specific address or individual MW figures were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
CyrusOne Sterling publishes 38 MW of IT capacity, placing it eleventh among Virginia's twenty-three facilities with disclosed power figures and representing roughly 950 racks at standard training density.

The facility occupies 700,000 square feet in Loudoun County's Ashburn corridor, part of Northern Virginia's dense cluster of data centers. Sterling's rank by published capacity reflects significant scale, though the operator does not disclose total campus capacity. The 38 MW IT load is therefore a floor, not a ceiling, on actual power draw.

At standard densities, 38 MW could support a substantial training cluster. The actual hardware composition remains unknown: GPU-heavy AI workloads run hotter and pack fewer racks per megawatt, while CPU or inference tasks run cooler and pack more. The published IT capacity cannot distinguish between these uses, so the rack estimate assumes uniform density across the site.

Sterling draws power from the same regional grid as 325 other mapped sites in Virginia, of which only 22 disclose their capacity. Grid interconnection status and any published certifications are absent from operator disclosures. This opacity is typical: Virginia's data center corridor is power-constrained but largely undocumented in aggregate.
